Answer: B
Reason: Figure 4b shows a prominent, tortuous vessel (indicated by arrows) descending along the left mediastinal border towards the left lower lobe, which is characteristic of an anomalous systemic arterial supply. Combined with the left lower lobe opacity seen in Figure 4a and the history of recurrent haemoptysis, this finding is most consistent with systemic arterialization of the left lung lower lobe without sequestration (also known as Pryce type I sequestration or anomalous systemic arterial supply to normal basal segments).
